events.title: Traditional Founding of Rome
events.description: According to tradition, Romulus founded the city of Rome on this date, an event later commemorated by the Romans with the festival of Parilia. The date was calculated by the Roman scholar Marcus Terentius Varro.
events.significance: Rome grew from a small settlement into the center of a vast empire whose law, language, engineering, and institutions shaped Western civilization. The date is still celebrated in Rome each year.

events.title: Henry VIII Becomes King of England
events.description: Henry VIII acceded to the English throne upon the death of his father, Henry VII. He was just shy of 18 years old and soon married Catherine of Aragon.
events.significance: His reign led to the English Reformation, the break with the Roman Catholic Church, the establishment of the Church of England, and major changes in the English state and religion.

events.title: Battle of San Jacinto
events.description: Texian forces under Sam Houston defeated the Mexican army commanded by General Antonio López de Santa Anna in about 18 minutes near present-day Houston. Santa Anna was captured the following day.
events.significance: The victory secured Texas independence from Mexico and led to the creation of the Republic of Texas, later contributing to its annexation by the United States and the Mexican-American War.

events.title: Death of Mark Twain
events.description: American author Samuel Langhorne Clemens, known as Mark Twain, died at his home in Redding, Connecticut, at age 74. He was the author of The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.
events.significance: Twain is considered one of the greatest American writers, often called the father of American literature, and his works remain central to discussions of American society, humor, and race.

events.title: Birth of Queen Elizabeth II
events.description: Princess Elizabeth Alexandra Mary was born in Mayfair, London. She became queen in 1952 following the death of her father, George VI.
events.significance: Elizabeth II became the longest-reigning British monarch, reigning for over 70 years, and presided over the transformation of the empire into the Commonwealth and decades of social change.
